laws.statement: Two processes are never in the critical section together.
When the lock refuses a request, a live process is in the critical section.
A process in the critical section keeps the lock until its own release or its own exit.

mutants.description: The lock stores the pid alone as the owner identity.
The lock always decides that the owner is dead.

assumptions: The kernel gives a new start token to each process start.
Only acquire and release change the lock record.
Each event is atomic. There is no torn write and no crash inside an event.
Events occur one at a time. There is no concurrent step.
A process that exits does not release the lock.

link.note: The laws are proved on a model. No test compares the model with production lock code.
